title: Replication, partitioning, hot keys, consistent hashing
summary: Scaling past one box: leader/follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication, sync vs async and failover, replication lag anomalies and fixes, partitioning schemes, consistent hashing, rebalancing, hot keys, secondary indexes across partitions, and sizing a sharded replicated deployment.

labs.title: Consistent-hash ring with virtual nodes and rebalancing stats
Replicated KV with leader/follower and a lag simulator

units.title: Hot keys, secondary indexes and putting it together

outcomes.text: Explain leader/follower log shipping (log positions, in-order apply, bootstrapping) and choose between physical, logical and statement-based replication

Choose between asynchronous, semi-synchronous and synchronous replication given RPO, latency and availability, compute async RPO from lag and write rate, and describe failover, lost writes, split brain and fencing
Implement a replicated KV store with in-order followers, synchronous waiting and failover that promotes the most up-to-date follower and reports lost writes (labs/a4/replkv)
Diagnose read-your-writes, monotonic-reads and consistent-prefix anomalies from replica lag and implement and defend the fixes: leader windows, LSN tokens, floors, sticky sessions (labs/a4/replkv)
Explain multi-leader and leaderless replication, why last-write-wins loses data, how CRDT merges and home-region routing avoid conflicts, and why cross-record invariants need coordination
Choose a partitioning scheme (range, hash, directory, composite) from the access pattern and quantify the resharding cost of mod N versus consistent hashing
Implement a consistent-hash ring with virtual nodes, weights, N-replica lookup on distinct nodes, movement and balance statistics, bounded loads and rendezvous/jump-hash alternatives (labs/a4/ring)
Plan and operate rebalancing: fixed partitions vs dynamic splitting vs tokens, live migration with a short cutover, routing with epochs and redirects, and skew monitoring
Diagnose hot keys and celebrity problems, choose among caching, key splitting, write coalescing and data-model changes, and detect hot keys with heavy-hitter summaries
Choose between local and global secondary indexes, compute scatter-gather tail latency (1 - 0.99^N), and outline cross-partition query and transaction options
Size a sharded, replicated deployment from estimates (partitions, replication factor, failure domains, rebalancing headroom) and defend it under an AZ loss at peak
Implement a Space-Saving / Count-Min hot-key detector and a key-splitting router (labs/a4/hotkey)
Demonstrate last-write-wins data loss versus CRDT merging and explain the leaderless mechanisms: hinted handoff, read repair, anti-entropy
